requirement_text: "We require the SAT or the ACT for both prospective first year and transfer students." "We do not require the ACT writing or science sections or the SAT optional essay." Tests must be completed by November 30 (Early Action) or December 31 (Regular Action). MIT superscores both the SAT and ACT. Reinstated March 28, 2022 (announced by the Dean of Admissions) for the Class of 2027 onward -- MIT suspended testing only for the pandemic-affected Classes of 2025 and 2026 and never adopted an indefinite test-optional stance.
researcher_notes: MIT was the first elite US institution to reverse a pandemic-era test-optional stance (2022) -- its testing-required posture has been stable and public since, unlike several peer institutions (Brown, Cornell) whose requirement is more recently reinstated (2024).

requirement_text: Recommended (not strictly required) for non-native English speakers who have used English fewer than 5 years or don't speak it at home/school. Accepted: Cambridge English (C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency), Duolingo English Test, IELTS, PTE Academic, TOEFL. Minimum / Recommended scores: TOEFL before 2026-01-21: 90 / 100; TOEFL from 2026-01-21: 5 / 5.5 (ETS redesigned scale); IELTS: 7 / 7.5; PTE Academic: 65 / 70; Cambridge: 185 / 190; Duolingo: 120 / 125.
scope: undergraduate (first-year) applicants -- MIT's graduate-level English proficiency policy differs by department and is not this record's subject
researcher_notes: Fifth confirmed sighting of the identical ETS TOEFL 21-Jan-2026 rescale boundary (after USC/Purdue in top-5, Loughborough in next-10) -- MIT's page is also the first to explicitly publish both a minimum AND a separate recommended score per test, a more granular structure than any prior sighting.
test_scale: dual: legacy 0-120 TOEFL scale pre-2026-01-21, new ETS scale post-2026-01-21

requirement_text: "Brown has returned to its previous policy requiring standardized test scores -- either SAT or ACT scores -- for first-year applicants beginning with the 2024-25 admission cycle." Brown accepts Score Choice and superscores both the SAT and ACT; states it has no minimum test score required for admission.

Not a single flat figure: requirements are organised into named "profiles" (e.g. Profile 3-D, 1-D, 2-M, 7-D) that vary by faculty/subject, each with its own list of acceptable tests and scores. One concrete confirmed example: the English BA programme requires "an overall IELTS score of 8.0, with a minimum score of 8.0 in each component (Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking)" -- among the highest single-test thresholds found across both this package and the prior two. IELTS scores carry a recommended two-year validity period, enforced by the university.
scope: subject/profile-dependent -- no single university-wide number exists
limitations: The general/standard-profile IELTS number (the one most applicants would fall under) was not locatable this pass -- the official page links out to per-profile sub-pages rather than stating one on the landing page itself; only the English BA's unusually high 8.0/8.0 figure was directly confirmed as a concrete data point.
researcher_notes: Worth flagging to counselor-facing content: St Andrews' profile system means 'St Andrews requires IELTS 6.5' (a figure floating around several secondary/aggregator sources) is not a reliable claim -- the actual number is subject-dependent and can run considerably higher (8.0 for English).

requirement_text: Test-optional "for applicants for admission in the fall semester of 2027" -- "Students who are unable to or who elect not to submit their test scores will have the requirement automatically waived and will not be penalized." WashU is also introducing a new Early Action option (alongside existing ED I / ED II / Regular Decision) starting with the Fall 2027 cycle, and now considers demonstrated interest.
source_authority_note: Corroborated via WebSearch summarizing WashU's own admissions announcements page and a WashU student-newspaper (Student Life) report on the same policy change -- not independently re-fetched with a raw quote this pass.
researcher_notes: The new Early Action option is a genuine, dated policy change for the Fall 2027/Class-of-2031 cycle, not a standing feature -- worth noting if the product surfaces 'application plans' per institution, since older secondary sources will still list only ED I/ED II/RD for WashU.

requirement_text: "You're required to submit SAT or ACT scores when applying to Cornell." Applies across all eight of Cornell's undergraduate colleges. Reinstated for students enrolling fall 2026 and beyond. International applicants must additionally "demonstrate English language proficiency and may be required to submit scores from an approved English language proficiency exam."
limitations: The specific approved English-proficiency exams and minimum scores for international applicants are on a linked sub-page not fetched this pass.

requirement_text: "The UW no longer requires SAT or ACT scores for most applicants." Explicit exception: "Homeschooled applicants and applicants who come from schools with non-standard grading practices that do not have letter or numeric grades are still required to submit SAT or ACT scores."
scope: general test-optional, with a named carve-out for homeschooled/non-standard-grading applicants
researcher_notes: The homeschooled/non-standard-grading carve-out is a distinct, previously-unseen exception shape across both prior packages -- not a blanket test-optional policy the way Rochester/Emory/UVA/BU state theirs.

requirement_text: Non-EU/EEA international applicants to Bachelor's programmes must complete TestAS (an aptitude test administered in German) before applying. All programmes additionally require certified English language proficiency where relevant: "TOEFL internet-based minimum of 90 points or paper-based minimum of 577 points" (figure confirmed for Master's-level pages; not independently re-confirmed on a Bachelor's-specific page this pass). Restricted-admission (Numerus Clausus / NC) programmes run a separate selection/lottery process, distinct from open-admission programmes.
scope: non-EU/EEA applicants; NC-restricted programmes have additional selection criteria beyond this record
limitations: The official Bachelor's international-applicants page was fetched directly but did not itself state the TOEFL minimum or TestAS requirement in the fetched excerpt -- those specifics came from WebSearch synthesis of RWTH's Master's-level pages and secondary aggregators, not confirmed as identical for Bachelor's level. Flagged NEEDS_REVIEW; RWTH's Bachelor programmes are also predominantly German-taught, so a German-language proficiency requirement (not captured here) may be the more commonly-applicable one for most programmes rather than TOEFL/English.
researcher_notes: Weakest-sourced requirement record in this batch, similar in kind to Leicester/City-St-George's/UVA in the prior package -- genuine German-language-proficiency figures for RWTH Bachelor's admission were not located this pass and should be the priority for any follow-up on this institution.

requirement_text: "Boston University has decided to remain test optional for students applying for admission through fall 2028 and spring 2029." Applies across all undergraduate schools/colleges and all scholarship programs. BU accepts self-reported scores on the application, with official scores submitted later via testing agency or the MyBU Applicant Portal self-report form if the applicant chooses to submit at all.
researcher_notes: BU's stated horizon (through fall 2028/spring 2029) is unusually long relative to peer institutions' typical one-cycle-at-a-time extensions (Rochester 'through at least fall 2027', Emory/WashU 'for Fall 2027').

requirement_text: "Starting with the Fall 2024-25 admission cycle, Rice recommends, but does not require, that students submit SAT or ACT test scores." Rice practices holistic review, does not use cutoffs or minimum test scores, and states applicants who don't submit scores "will still receive full consideration."
limitations: Not independently re-fetched with a raw quote from the blog post itself this pass -- WebSearch-synthesized from the official domain.
researcher_notes: Distinct policy category from strict 'test-optional' (Rochester/Emory/BU/WashU/UW) -- Rice frames it as 'recommended,' a softer version of Purdue's 'test expected' shape from the top-5 package but explicitly holistic/no-cutoff, worth its own value in a typed enum if the product builds one.
